question_en:
While organizing training materials for poll workers, we found this screenshot of an electronic ballot interface. Please answer the following questions:

1. Which agency published the document containing this interface, and what is the document? Provide the agency name, full document title, section name, publication date, and the formal name of the screen sample shown in the image.
2. Within the scope of all named complete screen samples appearing before **Settings** and **Alternate settings** in that section, identify the samples where the outermost active interface directly displays a blue checkmark. Do not count pages dimmed behind a pop-up window or diagrams embedded in help pages. How many screens meet these criteria? List the printed page number and formal name of each qualifying screen in ascending order of page number.

Response Format: Answer in two parts labeled (1) and (2). For question 1, present the requested information in a two-column table with headers "Item" and "Answer". For question 2, state the count in text, and then list the page number and formal name of all matching screens in a table ordered by printed page number.
answer:
(1)

| Item | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Agency Name | U.S. Election Assistance Commission (EAC) |
| Full Document Title | Effective Designs for the Administration of Federal Elections |
| Section Name | Section 5: Rolling DRE ballots |
| Publication Date | June 2007 |
| Formal Name of Screen Sample in Image | Contest screen, single selection |

(2) There are 4 screens that meet the criteria.

| Printed Page Number | Formal Name |
| --- | --- |
| 5.25 | Contest screen, single selection |
| 5.26 | Contest screen, multiple selections with scrolling |
| 5.27 | Ballot measures screen, no scrolling |
| 5.28 | Review screen |

## Step 01 · Read interface features from the current ballot screenshot

**Action**: Observe top auxiliary buttons, candidate list, and checked items; example query: "Austin Hildebrand" "James Garritty" ballot design.

**Evidence Observation**: The input image has Audio, Text size, Help, Review your choices; the row with Austin Hildebrand and James Garritty shows a blue checkmark. It is an electronic voting interface sample; the image itself does not state the publishing agency or full report name.

**Evidence Links**:

https://www.eac.gov/sites/default/files/eac_assets/1/6/Rolling_DRE_ballots.PDF

**Result of this step**: Use unique candidate text and layout to locate official design materials.

## Step 02 · Verify EAC report and section attribution

**Action**: Read the EAC polling place materials design page, check the Rolling DRE Ballots download entry and the report title and publication date.

**Evidence Observation**: The official page lists this PDF as a section of Effective Designs for the Administration of Federal Elections, with a publication date of Published June2007. The document's first page lists U.S. Election Assistance Commission, Section5, and Rolling DRE ballots.

**Evidence Links**:

https://www.eac.gov/election-officials/designing-polling-place-materials

https://www.eac.gov/sites/default/files/eac_assets/1/6/Rolling_DRE_ballots.PDF

**Evidence Observation**: The sample at the top of printed page 5.25 is Contest screen, single selection; it matches the attachment's single-selection president/vice-president combination and the checkmark positions for Austin Hildebrand and James Garritty.
